AT THIS CONTACT
  Presentation and contacts:
    - A 30 year old female presented to the neurology out patients department
  Course and symptoms:
    - cramps, rigidity, tremor and twitching and abnormal movements of hands and feet
    - The patient complained that this problem was continuing despite treatment for 6 years
  Examination and investigations:
    - A CT scan of brain (done outside) revealed basal ganglia calcification
    - Non contrast CT scan of brain showing calcification
  Treatments and response:
    - she was being treated with antiepileptics [eptoin 100mg bid] along with vitamin E [Evion 400mg od]

AT THIS CONTACT
  Presentation and contacts:
    - She was referred to Endocrinology department
  Background and exposures:
    - She was married for twelve years, had her first child six years back, who died at 6 months of age due to high grade fever
    - Two years later, she had a son
    - She was employed in a bangle making factory, and had to give up her job due to this recurring health problem
    - Patient never had surgery or irradiation of neck
  Course and symptoms:
    - Six months after delivery, she began to experience convulsions, tetany, stiffness of hands and feet and would fall down, and then recover completely on her own, in a few minutes
    - This happened about twice or thrice a month
    - She had long standing generalized weakness
  Examination and investigations:
    - While in the OPD, two bouts of tetany were witnessed by the doctor, followed by recovery in a few minutes
    - On examination, she weighed 32 kg, height 144 cm, and blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg
    - All other systems were normal on examination
    - Findings from an electroencephalogram were normal

AT THIS CONTACT
  Background and exposures:
    - A 12-year-old Bahraini girl was born at Salmaniya Medical Complex at full term through vaginal delivery, with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes
    - The mother's age during pregnancy was 38 years
  Family history:
    - The patient was the fifth child of consanguineous parents who had four other healthy daughters and had one abortion
    - Family pedigree of the child.
  Examination and investigations:
    - A prenatal sonography performed in the last trimester showed a congenital abnormality affecting the nose
    - After delivery with a birth weight of 2,640 g, the patient's physical examination revealed dysmorphic features in the form of hypoplastic alae nasi, microcephaly, mild hypotelorism, and cutis aplasia on the scalp
    - Eye examination was normal
    - Other systemic examinations were unremarkable
    - The child's dysmorphic features soon after delivery.

AT THIS CONTACT
  Course and symptoms:
    - The parents observed abdominal distention, oily foul-smelling stools, and nonbilious, nonprojectile vomiting after each feeding
    - Moreover, delayed growth was also detected and manifested as poor weight and height gains
    - the patient experienced a delay in reaching developmental milestones as she started first rolling over at the age of one year and walking at the age of one and a half years
  Examination and investigations:
    - The patient underwent extensive evaluation by multiple medical teams, including specialists in neonatology, otorhinolaryngology, plastic surgery, endocrinology, radiology, and genetics
    - Laboratory results showed a hemoglobin level of 9.2 g/dL with low indices
    - Serum electrolytes, calcium, phosphorus, urea, creatinine, liver function tests, and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase levels were all within the normal range
    - A stool fat globules test was positive, but fecal tryptic activity was normal with a dilution of 1:3200; pancreatic insufficiency is considered if fecal tryptic activity dilution is less than 1:50
    - Abdominal ultrasound, echocardiogram, and brain magnetic resonance imaging were all reported to be normal
    - Hearing assessment was done using an auditory brainstem response test, which showed no response up to 100 dB normal hearing level in both ears
    - Given dysmorphism, the genetic specialist requested genetic testing, and blood samples of the child and both parents were sent to Germany
    - The microarray study showed a novel sequence change mutation of the UBR1 gene (1 bp duplication causing a frameshift)
    - Both parents were heterozygous carriers of this mutation
    - Furthermore, she had hypotonia, but her motor functions were normal
    - At the age of two years, serial imaging was obtained
    - An MRI of the spine, conducted as part of the brain and internal auditory meatus protocol, revealed an incidental, eccentrically placed cystic lesion at the anterior aspect of the spinal cord at the level of the second thoracic vertebra, most likely representing a syringohydromyelia
    - A brainstem auditory-evoked response trace showing no response at maximum auditory stimulation (100 dB nHL) in both ears, which indicates a bilateral profound hearing loss
    - World Health Organization growth charts showing the anthropometric parameters: weight-for-age and length/height-for-age from birth to 10 years
    - A sagittal T2-weighted MRI of the spine: a hyperintense cystic lesion at the anterior aspect of the spinal cord at the second thoracic vertebral level, most likely representing a syringohydromyelia
    - Laboratory results: haemoglobin 9.2 g/dL at age 0.2 falling to 8.2 at age 12, MCV 73.5 to 57.9, iron 6.0-3.0 umol, transferrin saturation 6-3%, persistent lymphocytosis; subclinical hypothyroidism
  Treatments and response:
    - This confirmed the diagnosis of JBS
    - Shortly after delivery, the patient commenced combined breast and formula milk feeding
    - The patient was started on pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (Creon 1 capsule per kilogram), fat-soluble vitamins, minerals, and antioxidant syrup along with dietary advice to transition to a specialized anti-regurgitation milk formula
    - Thereafter, the patient required regular follow-up and management by a pediatric gastroenterology consultant
    - However, further clinical correlation to assess for upper limb muscle tone and follow-up with an MRI was advised
    - At the age of three years, the patient underwent sequential bilateral cochlear implantation
    - Postoperatively, aural rehabilitation with the speech therapist was provided, and she had to wear bilateral external sound processors
  Recorded working diagnosis:
    - Based on clinical presentation and laboratory results, a diagnosis of pancreatic insufficiency was confirmed

AT THIS CONTACT
  Background and exposures:
    - The patient had not traveled in the last year and had no contact with any unwell person or anyone with tuberculosis
    - He did not drink alcohol and did not use recreational drugs apart from occasionally smoking shisha
  Family history:
    - The patient had no family history of cardiac diseases or autoimmune conditions but did have a first-degree relative (brother is known to have FMF with episodic chest pain currently on colchicine), and consanguinity of his parents
  Course and symptoms:
    - despite being compliant with his treatment, the patient presented to our hospital (two days after discharge) with worsening sharp pleuritic chest pain radiating to the left shoulder
    - The pain was worse when lying flat and better when sitting up
    - The patient denied any shortness of breath, palpitations, or syncope
    - The patient did feel dizzy on occasion but had no heart failure symptoms
    - The patient had never experienced chest pain symptoms like this in the past, and there was no history of recent viral illnesses, diarrhea or vomiting, any weight loss, or night sweats
  Examination and investigations:
    - His troponin and D-dimer were both negative, and his inflammatory markers were raised
    - The examination was largely unremarkable. He was warm and well-perfused, on auscultation his lungs were clear, and he had normal heart sounds with no pericardial or pleural rub
    - The abdominal examination was normal, and his calves were soft and non-tender
    - There were no signs of heart failure, no other stigmata of systemic disease, lymphadenopathy, or pharyngitis
  Treatments and response:
    - with colchicine and ibuprofen, and he discharged himself against medical advice the next day
  Recorded working diagnosis:
    - he was treated for presumed pericarditis

AT THIS CONTACT
  Background and exposures:
    - A 61-year-old Caucasian man with a past medical history of hyperlipidemia, obesity (BMI 37 kg/m2), and osteoarthritis
    - Prior to surgery, the patient led an active lifestyle, including regular elliptical use and golfing
    - Following his knee arthroplasty he attended all physical therapy sessions
  Course and symptoms:
    - One month following surgery, he abruptly became lightheaded and dyspneic, with no relief of symptoms upon rest
  Examination and investigations:
    - He presented to his local emergency department where he was noted to have sinus tachycardia and hypoxia
  Treatments and response:
    - underwent a left knee arthroplasty without complication
    - After undergoing surgery, he received DVT prophylaxis with two days of low molecular weight heparin while hospitalized and was then discharged home on 81 mg of aspirin daily

AT THIS CONTACT
  Presentation and contacts:
    - The patient presented to our center's chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension clinic approximately three and a half months after his submassive pulmonary embolism because of persistent symptoms of postural dizziness and chest pain
  Background and exposures:
    - He had no history of prior pulmonary emboli or deep venous thrombi and no known risk factors for VTE, other than recent surgery
    - the patient developed a DVT in the contralateral leg, making it unlikely that recent orthopedic surgery alone accounted for his significant VTE burden
    - His risk factors for pulmonary hypertension included obesity, recreational methamphetamine use 40 years prior to presentation, and anorexigen use for six months 20 years prior to presentation
    - Surgical history was notable for left knee and hip replacements
    - He denied current tobacco or drug use and drank one glass of wine per day
  Family history:
    - His family history was notable for one brother who had a pulmonary embolism
  Course and symptoms:
    - He also reported paraesthesias along the back of his head, legs, and feet
    - His ongoing symptoms were limiting his participation in these activities, and he was unable to return to work as a hospital food service director
  Examination and investigations:
    - CT pulmonary angiogram revealed a large saddle pulmonary embolism with an extension of the clot into multiple lobar and segmental branches
    - Cardiac enzymes were normal and EKG showed no ischemic changes
    - NT-pro-BNP was elevated at 154 pg/mL
    - Transthoracic echocardiogram showed moderately increased right ventricular size with moderately depressed right ventricular systolic function, and mild pulmonary hypertension, consistent with the diagnosis of submassive pulmonary embolism
    - During his hospital stay, he also had a Doppler ultrasound of the lower extremities revealing a non-occlusive deep venous thrombosis in the right popliteal and peroneal veins and a head CT due to dizziness which showed no acute process
    - The physical exam at this time was normal
    - Representative images of initial CT pulmonary angiography demonstrating acute pulmonary emboli with saddle pulmonary emboli extending into the right upper lobe (A) and right lower lobe (B) pulmonary arteries
  Treatments and response:
    - He received high-flow nasal cannula and heparin and was admitted to the ICU
    - He remained hemodynamically stable and supplemental oxygen was weaned
    - Intravenous anticoagulation therapy with heparin was transitioned to apixaban
    - He was discharged home on day 6

AT THIS CONTACT
  Presentation and contacts:
    - The patient was transferred clinically stable to a specific COVID-19 center where she was treated for 2 weeks with oral amoxicillin and clavulanic acid, intravenous PPI, and subcutaneous LMWH
  Examination and investigations:
    - Computed tomography angiography of the aorta and lower limbs revealed a floating thrombus in the abdominal aorta (length 3.8 cm, width 0.9 cm) with minimal marginal flow and iliac arteries of regular lumen width with marginal atherosclerotic plaques
    - Computed tomography angiography confirmed thromboembolism of the entire right deep femoral artery as well as in distal part of the left deep femoral artery
    - Furthermore, both superficial femoral arteries had a sustained flow
    - Third segment of the right popliteal artery was occluded with thromboembolus, spreading to the posterior tibial artery with marginal recanalization
    - Although the patient had no fever, respiratory, or any other typical COVID-19-associated symptoms, routine preoperative polymerase chain reaction test using throat and nasopharyngeal swabs came positive for SARS-CoV-2
    - a MSCT angiography of the aorta demonstrates an aortic thromboembolism, axial plane. b MSCT angiography of the aorta, coronal reconstruction.
  Treatments and response:
    - Successful surgical thromboembolectomy was performed after being confirmed by multislice computed tomography angiography
    - She was also treated with LMWH, proton pump inhibitor, analgesic therapy, cefuroxime, and transfusions of deplasmatized red blood cells
    - During hospitalization in the center, she was asymptomatic regarding SARS-CoV-2 infection recovering well from surgical intervention

  Background and exposures:
    - The patient denied using any hepatotoxic substances except rivaroxaban
  Course and symptoms:
    - Four months after discharge, the patient was admitted to the intensive care unit due to ALI of unknown etiology
    - Personal medical history included complaints of nausea in the past month as well as occurrence of jaundice a day before admission
  Examination and investigations:

  Background and exposures:

  Course and symptoms:
    - presented to emergency department with the complaint of loss of consciousness of 02 hours duration
    - Three days prior to her presentation, she started to have complaints of progressively worsening fatigue, poor oral intake, decreased urine output, appetite loss, vertigo and global headache
    - One day prior to her arrival, she had a single episode of watery diarrhea
    - She had no fever, chills, chest pain, dyspnea, or body swelling
  Examination and investigations:
    - On evaluation, the patient was lethargic with blood pressure of 60/40 mmHg, absent radial pulse, cold extremities and temperature of 36.4 C
    - Her examination was remarkable for dry buccal mucosa; apical heart rate was 22 beats per minute
    - On Central Nervous System examination, GCS was 13/15
    - The other system examinations were normal
  Treatments and response:
    - The family stated that she was taking atenolol 50 mg daily and Enalapril 10 mg daily properly till the time of her presentation

AT THIS CONTACT
  Course and symptoms:
    - An 18-year-old woman, with no significant medical history, seeks care for a one-year history of polymorphic and multifocal lesions with alternating periods of remission and exacerbation
  Examination and investigations:
    - At admission, the physical examination showed disseminated dermatosis
    - These lesions were characterized by multiple erythematous-violaceous plaques
    - Some of these plaques presented a central vesicle, hemorrhagic blisters, as well as hypo and hyperpigmented spots
    - In addition, in the lower limbs, she presented ulcers of different sizes with well-delimited violet edges, necrotic background, and some perilesional blisters
    - Clinical image: multiple infiltrated erythematous plaques, hemorrhagic vesicles and residual hypo- and hyperpigmented lesions scattered in the chest and abdomen; close-up of erythematous-violaceous plaque; close-up of hemorrhagic blister
    - Clinical image: multiple ulcers in the right lower limb of different sizes and depths; close-up of an ulcer with violaceous edges, well defined and irregular, with a necrotic background and a perilesional blister; close-up of ulcer with exposure of gastrocnemius muscles

  Presentation and contacts:
    - On 27th July 2020 ... required a medical examination at our Occupational Health Dept.
  Background and exposures:
    - a 47-year-old woman, working as a ceramic dental technician since November 2018
    - Owing to the SARS-CoV2 pandemic, she was absent from workplace from March 2020
    - At work, the woman was involved in milling and polishing monolithic zirconia structures, then layered with ceramic
    - She described workplace as dusty, lacking aspiration hoods hence she was concerned about workplace safety
    - She used respiratory personal protective equipment (PPE) inconstantly
  Course and symptoms:
    - in the previous months she was affected by dry and irritating cough, especially related to intense work activity
    - She also suffered some episodes of low-grade fever and fatigue and dyspnea on efforts
    - in such period her symptoms ameliorated
  Examination and investigations:
    - Pulmonary function tests were in the normality range and revealed a normal diffusing capacity, albeit at the lower limits of the normal (DLCO/VA 73%); autoimmunity markers were in the normal range

AT THIS CONTACT
  Presentation and contacts:
    - A 40-year-old female patient came to our attention from the emergency room for a clinical study of a severe form of hypertension
  Background and exposures:
    - She didn't take any drugs or homeopathic products, had no history of allergies, didn't smoke
  Family history:
    - had no family history of cardiovascular disease
  Course and symptoms:
    - associated with dizziness, gait instability, and diffuse cramps
  Examination and investigations:
    - On these occasions, clinical and neurological examinations were stated to be unremarkable, and a CT scan of the head showed no abnormalities
    - Her past medical history included only a recent biopsy for a breast nodule identified as a local lymphocytic vasculitis
    - Once hospitalized in our clinic, during physical examination, we found an abdominal bruit and diminished peripheral (femoral and tibial) pulses bilaterally
    - Blood pressure (BP) ranged between 200/110 mmHg and 180/100 mmHg during the hospital stay
    - Other vital signs were normal
    - A 24-hour continuous monitoring of blood pressure revealed a BP mean value of 183/97 mmHg with a non-dipper profile
    - The main findings were decreased potassium (which was refractory to supplementation), impaired renal function, and minimal elevation of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate
    - Further testing has been done to exclude secondary causes of hypertension, revealing a significant increase in renin and aldosterone with a low aldosterone/renin ratio
    - Laboratory test for the diagnostic workup of secondary hypertension: potassium 2.90 mMol/L, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, ESR 17 mm/h, aldosterone 146.0 ng/dL, renin 1203.0 uUI/mL, aldosterone/renin ratio 0.12, ANA negative, urinary aldosterone 90.5 ug/24h
  Treatments and response:
    - therefore, the patient was discharged with advice to monitor blood pressure at home and book a cardiological evaluation
  Recorded working diagnosis:
    - In light of these findings, we suspected renovascular hypertension
